plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plain vector diagram of four arrows stacked one above another, all drawn at the same shallow upward slope so their lengths can be compared at a glance. Each arrow starts from a small filled black dot. The topmost arrow, in dark navy, is by far the longest and is labeled 3v at its head. Below it an orange arrow labeled v runs in the same up-and-to-the-right direction at about a third that length. Beneath the orange one, a teal arrow labeled 1/2 v is half as long as v and again points the same way. The bottom arrow, drawn in red and labeled -v, has its dot at the right end and its arrowhead at the left, so it runs down and to the left while staying parallel to the others and matching v in length. Because all four share a single line of action, the only difference the eye registers is length, plus the reversal in the last one. The arrangement gives the geometric reading of multiplying a vector by a scalar: a positive factor stretches or shrinks the arrow while preserving its heading, and a negative factor turns it back on itself.

interactionPlan.concept: Multiplying a vector by a scalar k stretches or shrinks its length by |k| while keeping the same line of action — and reverses its direction when k is negative.
elements: Four parallel arrows stacked vertically, all drawn at the same shallow upward-right slope (roughly 15–20°)
Small filled black dot marking the tail (initial point) of each arrow
Dark navy arrow, longest, labeled '3v' in bold italic at its arrowhead (top of stack)
Orange arrow of reference length, labeled 'v' in bold italic near its head (second from top)
Teal arrow, half the reference length, labeled '½v' (fraction stacked) near its head (third)
Red arrow equal in length to v but reversed: black dot at the right end, arrowhead at the lower-left, labeled '−v' to the right of the dot (bottom)
Optional overlay mode: a single shared tail dot with all scaled arrows radiating along one common line of action
Optional faint dashed guide line through the shared line of action in overlay mode
Optional readout showing the current scalar k, the resulting vector's component form, and its magnitude |k||v|
Optional tick marks / faint length ruler along the line of action showing multiples of |v|

interactions.teaches: That the arrow's length is |k| times the original, that direction is preserved for k>0 and flipped for k<0, and that the vector collapses to a point at k=0.
interactions.label: Scalar multiplier k

interactions.teaches: That the stacked view makes lengths easy to compare, while the shared-tail overlay makes it obvious that every scalar multiple lies on one line through the tail — same ray for positive k, opposite ray for negative k.
interactions.label: Arrow layout

interactions.teaches: Lets the learner isolate the live kv arrow against the fixed reference set 3v, v, ½v, −v to check where their scaled vector lands.
interactions.label: Show live kv arrow

demo_steps.title: The reference vector v
demo_steps.narration: Start with the orange arrow v and its three relatives stacked above and below it. Every arrow points along the same shallow upward slope, so only length and direction-sign differ.

demo_steps.title: Stretching: k = 3
demo_steps.narration: Drag k up to 3 and the live arrow grows to three times the length of v, matching the navy 3v arrow exactly — but its heading never changes.

demo_steps.title: Shrinking: k = ½
demo_steps.narration: Pull k down to one half and the arrow contracts onto the teal ½v. A scalar between 0 and 1 shortens the vector without tilting it.

demo_steps.title: Crossing zero
demo_steps.narration: At k = 0 the arrow shrinks to a single point at the tail — the zero vector. Nudging k just below zero makes the arrowhead pop out on the opposite side.

demo_steps.title: Reversing: k = −1
demo_steps.narration: At k = −1 the arrow has the same length as v but points down and to the left, matching the red −v arrow. Negative scalars reverse direction along the same line.

demo_steps.title: Overlay: one line of action
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the shared-tail overlay: all the arrows now spring from one dot. Positive multiples stack along one ray, the negative multiple lies on the opposite ray — every scalar multiple of v lives on a single line.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Scalar multiplication changes only how far you travel along a fixed line — |k| sets the length, and the sign of k picks which of the two directions along that line you go.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: White background, four arrows stacked from top to bottom, all parallel at a shallow upward-right slope of roughly 15–20°, each beginning at a small filled black dot. Top: dark navy arrow spanning nearly the full width, labeled '3v' in bold italic just past its arrowhead at upper right. Second: orange arrow about one third that length, labeled 'v' in bold italic above its head. Third: teal arrow half the orange one's length, labeled '½v' with a stacked fraction above its head. Bottom: red arrow equal in length to the orange one but reversed — black dot on the right, arrowhead at lower left, label '−v' just right of the dot. Keep arrowheads solid and proportional to line weight; line weight is uniform across all four. The live kv arrow should be drawn in a distinct accent color (e.g. purple) with a small 'kv' label and its tail on the same black dot as v in stacked mode. In overlay mode, collapse all tails onto one dot near the lower-left with a faint dashed guide line extended through it in both directions; arrowheads then terminate at distances proportional to their scale factors, positive multiples to the upper right and negative ones to the lower left. A small text readout of k and |kv| may sit in a corner.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for scalar multiplier k: the learner drags k from negative to positive values, the arrow length scales and flips direction when k crosses 0, and scalar multiplication is seen as stretching, shrinking, or reversing a vector.
- Toggle between stacked comparison and overlay: the learner switches from separate arrows to all arrows sharing the same tail, the endpoints line up by scale factor, and equal direction for positive multiples versus opposite direction for negative multiples becomes easier to read.

discrepancies: At the default (step-0) state a translucent purple 'k v' arrow is drawn exactly on top of the orange v arrow, with a purple 'k v' label sitting immediately beside the source's 'v' label — an added element that makes the drop-in state look doubled/cluttered compared with the clean source figure.
A grey numeric readout ('k = 1.00  k v = ⟨3.00, 1.00⟩  |k v| = |k||v| = 3.16') is placed at the top-left of the canvas; nothing like it exists in the source.

The '3v' arrow in the source nearly spans the full figure width starting from a tail low on the left; the generated version is slightly shorter/steeper in placement, and the 3v label sits closer to the tip than in the source, but the overall composition still reads correctly.
Tail dots in the generated figure are slightly larger/heavier than the small black dots in the source (minor).
evaluation.notes: The four stacked scalar-multiple arrows, their colors, slopes, relative lengths and labels (3v, v, ½v, −v) reproduce the source closely and the slider/toggle/demo-step interactions are meaningful and correct; the main weakness is the extra purple live 'k v' arrow plus its label and the numeric readout cluttering the default state that should read as a drop-in replacement.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; only execution details need fixing — hide the overlapping purple 'k v' arrow/label and numeric readout in the default state and tune arrow geometry/dot sizes.

discrepancies: Arrow stroke weight and tail-dot radius are noticeably heavier than in the source, giving the generated figure a bolder, chunkier look than the thin vectors of the original.

Label typography differs: the generated '3v', 'v', '½v', '−v' are larger, bolder Georgia italics than the source's smaller serif italics, and '3v' sits almost on top of the navy arrowhead rather than clearly above-right of it.
The UI panel text wraps badly ('Scalar multiplier k' / ':' / '1.00' on three lines; 'Show live k v arrow' split over four lines), which reads as broken labelling even though the controls work.

Minor composition shift: the teal ½v arrow and red −v arrow sit slightly lower/right relative to the frame than in the source, and the red arrow is somewhat longer than v whereas the source draws it about the same length.
evaluation.notes: Default state is an excellent near drop-in replacement for the source (correct four parallel arrows, matching colors, tail dots, and 3v / v / ½v / −v labels), backed by genuinely meaningful interactions (k slider, live kv arrow, shared-tail overlay, 6-step narrated demo); only minor stroke-weight, label-size and control-panel text-wrapping blemishes hold it back.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items remain and all core scores are 4.7–5 with only cosmetic stroke-weight and label-wrapping blemishes, so further iteration isn't warranted.
